entities.summary: Heo Im was a Korean acupuncturist of the Hayang Heo clan during the reign of King Seonjo of the Joseon period. Heo was known for his contribution to the development of acupuncture. His father, Heo Eok-bok (허억복) was a commoner from Yangyang and he was well known for his ability to work with flute and as a vocalist. His mother was a noble, the 7th descendant of Heo Jo (許租,허조) who was the civil minister during the reign of King Sejong. In 1609, he received a decree and was appointed to the office of the Majeun Military Commander, but this was then opposed by the Ministry of Social Welfare because of Im's status as a commoner.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Heo Im's contribution to the development of acupuncture had a significant impact on traditional Korean medicine, influencing its practice for centuries. His appointment as Majeun Military Commander in 1609 highlights his importance in Joseon society.
